title: Delean-Botkin resigns from Talbot Board of Education
content:
Susan Delean‑Botkin resigned from the Talbot County Board of Education on Aug 4 2023 after being appointed an Oxford Commissioner. She had served on the Board since Jan 2017, was elected president in Dec 2020 and held that role through 2022. Delean‑Botkin said she left for personal reasons and her new local‑government post; she “misses the board tremendously” and praised it as a “fabulous experience.”  

She urged the Board to keep the county’s high graduation and low dropout rates, expand Career & Technical Education courses, implement the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future, and increase Advanced Placement participation.  

President Emily Jackson thanked her, noting her wisdom will be missed. Executive Assistant Charlene Gould noted the governor has been notified of the vacancy and will appoint a replacement until the Nov 2024 elections; interested candidates can apply to the Governor’s Appointments Office.  

Delean‑Botkin was appointed to replace Commissioner Brian Wells (who resigned June 27 after moving to Easton) by Commissioners Tom Costigan and Jimmy Jaramillo. She had previously lost a race to now‑Commissioner Katrina Greer. Delean‑Botkin describes her Oxford role as “challenging,” noting Oxford’s ~600 residents, water‑surrounded limits on growth, and a community that values quality of life.

title: Kent 4-H alumna Jill Bramble to lead National Council
content:
Jill Bramble, a Kent County, Md. 4‑H alumna, will begin as president and CEO of the National 4‑H Council on Aug. 18 2023 after an 18‑month externally led search; the board approved her unanimously.  Bramble has served the Council for nearly 20 years, rising from grant writer (joined May 2005) to senior vice president and chief development officer, then to executive vice president and chief growth officer in March 2022, and will succeed Jennifer Sirangelo (leaving after ten years to lead Points of Light).  

Her background includes a 1993 University of Colorado kinesiology degree (initial PT goal) and a 2001 master’s in nonprofit management from the University of Maryland, earned after volunteer work and a corporate‑fundraising role with the American Cancer Society.  She also worked at Just Cause Consultants in Chestertown under mentor Linda Walls.  Bramble’s family, the Frys of Fair Hill Farms near Chestertown (moved 1960), include grandparents Edwin “Pop” and Lorraine Fry, whose great‑grandmother Susan Clarkson Fry was a Montgomery County 4‑H volunteer.  Her nephews Reid and Owen are intermediate‑age 4‑Hers in the Kent Clover Calf Club; her first 4‑H project was the Peppermint Patty cow from Pop Fry.  Mentors she cites are UMD Extension agent John Hall, Laura Bradley, and families Debnam, Crow, Dulin, Lott, Moffett, and Hill; former club leader Pat Hill still displays a cross‑stitch 4‑H emblem she made.  

Kent County educator Beth Hill, 28 years with UMD Extension, praised Bramble’s leadership and noted her role in raising a $10,000 endowment in three years (now $86,000).  Bramble’s 4‑H tenure began in the Kennedyville Blue Banner Club (dairy, public speaking, photography, ambassador program) in the 1980s.  

The National 4‑H Council—a private‑sector nonprofit partner of Cooperative Extension—handles fundraising, brand, communications, and legal/ fiduciary services.  It serves 6 million youth (ages 5‑19) and 600,000 volunteers nationwide.  Bramble will work remotely from Bluffton, South Carolina, spending one week/month at Washington, DC headquarters, and invites Kent County residents to visit.  No conflicts of interest were disclosed.

title: Community invited to celebrate completion of KI Branch Library renovation
content: Queen Anne’s County Library will hold a ribbon‑cutting and dedication on Tuesday, Aug. 8 2023 at 2:30 p.m. to unveil the renovated Kent Island Branch. The expansion—financed by the State of Maryland, Maryland State Library Agency, Queen Anne’s County Commissioners, citizens and library supporters—adds a welcoming lobby, community meeting rooms equipped with modern AV technology, and a state‑of‑the‑art Makerspace with 3‑D printers, laser engravers, vinyl printers/cutters, sewing machines and craft supplies. Library director Janet Salazar said the new spaces aim to deepen community connections and broaden learning. After the ceremony, staff will give tours and demonstrate the Makerspace. The event celebrates the partnership of local and state agencies and honors community support.

title: New director hired at Chesapeake College in Cambridge
content: Lorelly Solano, a native of Costa Rica who earned a bachelor’s degree there, worked for an international flower exporter while completing a master’s in natural resources science at the University of Maryland (researching “green” roofs). She then earned a Ph.D. in public policy and urban affairs at the University of Delaware, where she reflected on applying urban‑area lessons to a rural setting. Solano began at Chesapeake College as an English‑as‑a‑Second‑Language instructor, later serving as academic and career adviser. On August 8, 2023, the Star Democrat announced she was hired as director of Chesapeake College’s Cambridge Center on Race Street in Cambridge, MD. The center, part of Dorchester County, offers transfer and career credit classes, workforce training, personal enrichment programs, meeting spaces, and houses the American Job Center. Solano aims to bring a student‑centered perspective to all services, expand community outreach, and position the center as a catalyst for the economic and social vitality of downtown Cambridge and the wider county.

title: Chrome City Ride raises $105K for Benedictine School
content: On July 28 2023, the 18th‑annual Chrome City Ride in Ridgely, MD, drew over 2,100 participants and more than 1,200 classic cars, street rods and motorcycles from six Maryland and Delaware rally points to the Benedictine School campus. Volunteers—chiefly Spud Blake—organized the event, with sponsorship from CPR Vintage Porsche (Easton), Outback Steakhouse (Annapolis), Rommel Harley‑Davidson Delmarva (Salisbury), Old Glory Harley‑Davidson, Hitchcock Autoworks, Callahan’s Gas & Appliance (Centreville) and Choptank Transport (Preston). The ride raised $105,000 + for Benedictine, which serves over 200 children and adults with developmental disabilities from MD, DE, WV, PA and VA. Since 2001 the event has raised more than $2 million from roughly 15,000 participants. Winners included an orange HD Turbo Road King bike; Ray Nails’ red/silver 1954 Pontiac Star Chief car; Kid’s Choice winners Donald Teat (grand‑champion Huckster) and Mike Ledbetter (Harley Davidson). New this year was an auction of a signed Paul Reed Smith electric guitar, all proceeds going to the school. Riders received collectible T‑shirts and enjoyed a barbecue from Famous Dave’s. The event featured Rockin’ Elvis music and a Sister’s Choice award. Notable attendees were Candy Clark, Cindy Williams, Bo Hopkins, area legislators, celebrity donors Jay Leno (five‑plus years) and a New Jersey collector (1941 Willys Pro Street Coupe, 2016). Benedictine earned 2018‑2020 NCASES accreditation—one of 26 national institutions—and teacher Lorraine Slama was named 2018 Educator of the Year.
